newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm, market buoyed by fund buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm, market buoyed by fund buying.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures followed crude futures higher to finish trading on Friday about $2 up on the day as fund buying swept through the market, brokers said.
The July gas oil contract last traded $2 higher at $163.75 a tonne with a widening crack spread seen attracting buyers.
IPE Brent tested resistance at $18.17 a barrel, briefly breaking through to $18.23 in the mid-afternoon, before settling back to trade $18.11, 26 cents higher on the day, at 1652 GMT.
"The market has been going sideways for a while so some of the longer-term moving averages may have crossed and caused the funds to come back in and buy," said a broker.
The New York Mercantile Exchange's front-month crude contract was also riding into positive territory, up 25 cents at $19.34.
Traders said financial funds have been short for some time and may be looking to cover before resuming bearish positions early next month.
IPE numbers were also boosted by heavy physical crude buying as traders covered July requirements early out of fear delays in the shipment of Iraqi barrels would leave the month tight.
Differentials on the wet market all firmed and demand was good, although benchmark Brent blend cargo was little talked.

The gains on Friday were described as largely technically inspired and flew in the face of market scepticism OPEC's deal at its Vienna meeting to freeze output quotas would do anything to limit over-supply on world oil markets.

Quota cheaters within the 11-nation cartel produce about two million barrels per day above the supposed 25.03 million bpd and ignore pleas for restraint. The meeting was seen as doing little to improve compliance.
Fundamentals were expected to reassert themselves, with the resumption of Iraqi exports next month and excess OPEC crude likely to weigh on the market, traders said.
